q: A user reports they can reach an internal file share but not any website by name. At which OSI layer does the most likely fault sit?
e: Reaching the file share proves Layers 1 through 4 are working. Name resolution is DNS, an application-layer protocol, so a top-down approach starting at Layer 7 finds this fastest.

q: Which OSI layer is responsible for fragmenting packets so they fit a downstream network with a smaller frame size?
e: Fragmentation and reassembly is a Layer 3 network layer function, alongside logical addressing and routing.

q: A technician says the problem is 'at the switching layer.' Which layer do they mean?
e: Switches forward on destination MAC address, which is the data link layer. Routing on IP is Layer 3.

q: A switch receives a frame for a destination MAC address that is not in its MAC address table. What does it do?
a: Floods the frame out all ports except the one it arrived on
Drops the frame and sends an error to the source
Forwards it to the default gateway
Holds the frame until an ARP reply arrives
e: Unknown unicast is flooded so the destination can be found. Once the switch learns that MAC, flooding stops for that address.

q: Which statement correctly distinguishes an IDS from an IPS?
a: An IDS sits out-of-band and alerts; an IPS sits in-line and can block
An IDS sits in-line and blocks; an IPS sits out-of-band and alerts
An IDS is host-based; an IPS is always network-based
An IDS uses signatures; an IPS only uses anomaly detection
e: Placement is the distinction. Because an IPS is in-line, a false positive stops legitimate traffic — which is why systems are usually run in detection mode first while they are tuned.

q: An organisation needs block-level storage that appears to servers as a directly attached disk. What should be deployed?
e: A SAN presents block-level storage over a Fibre Channel fabric, so it looks like a local disk. A NAS is file-level over Ethernet using SMB or NFS.

q: A stateful firewall permits a reply from a web server to the client's random source port 3355, but blocks an unsolicited inbound connection to that same port. Why?
a: The permitted traffic belongs to a session the internal host initiated
Port 3355 is a well-known port that is open by default
The firewall filters only on destination IP address
Outbound rules always take precedence over inbound rules
e: A stateful firewall tracks connection state. Return traffic for an internally initiated session is allowed; an unsolicited inbound connection to the same port is not.

q: Which traffic should QoS prioritise on a congested link?
a: An email with a large attachment
e: QoS prioritises delay-intolerant traffic. The payroll file is business-critical but tolerates delay and reordering; a voice call does not.

q: Under which cloud service model does the customer manage the operating system and applications while the provider manages virtualisation, servers and storage?
e: IaaS gives you the infrastructure and leaves the OS upward to you. PaaS also abstracts the OS and runtime; SaaS leaves you only your data and settings.

q: Which term describes the ability of cloud resources to both grow and shrink automatically as demand changes?
e: Scalability is the ability to grow. Elasticity adds automatic contraction — capacity in April that shrinks again in May.

q: A compromised virtual machine was destroyed automatically before the security team could examine it. Which cloud characteristic caused this problem?
e: Elastic environments tear down instances automatically, which conflicts with forensic evidence preservation. A physical machine would still be on the floor to investigate.

q: Which protocol uses both TCP and UDP on the same port number?
e: DNS uses UDP for ordinary queries and TCP for zone transfers and oversized responses, both on port 53.

q: A user needs their mail to stay synchronised across a phone and a laptop. Which protocol and port?
e: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises state across devices. POP3 downloads and typically removes mail, so it suits only a single device.

q: Which pair of protocols is most often confused, despite being unrelated?
e: SFTP is SSH File Transfer Protocol on port 22 — a different protocol entirely. FTPS is FTP wrapped in TLS on 989/990. The other pairs are genuinely the same protocol secured.

q: In the DHCP DORA exchange, which message does the client broadcast first?
e: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge. Because Discover is a broadcast and broadcasts do not cross routers, a server on another subnet needs a relay agent or IP helper address.

q: Two switches must be connected and neither supports auto-MDIX. Which cable is required?
e: Like devices need a crossover so senders align with receivers. Different device types — PC to switch, switch to router — use straight-through.

q: Which multimode fibre category supports 40 Gbps up to 300 metres?
e: OM3 is 40 Gbps to 300 m; OM4 is 40 Gbps to 550 m. OM1 and OM2 are 10 Gbps at 33 m and 82 m.

q: Why must UPC and APC fibre connectors never be intermixed?
a: They will not work correctly and the connectors can be physically destroyed
APC carries data only in one direction
UPC is single-mode only and APC is multimode only
e: The end faces are polished differently — APC at an 8 degree angle — so they do not mate. They are colour-coded specifically to prevent this.

q: A run must carry 10 Gbps over the full 100 metres. Which cabling meets that?
e: Cat 6 carries 10 Gbps only to about 55 m. Cat 7 sustains 10 Gbps over the full 100 m.

q: In a spine-leaf data centre fabric, why is Spanning Tree Protocol unnecessary between leaf and spine?
a: Those links run at Layer 3, where loop prevention does not require blocking links
Spine-leaf uses only a single link between each pair of switches
STP is replaced by link aggregation on all fabric links
Leaf switches operate in half duplex, which prevents loops
e: Leaf-to-spine connectivity is Layer 3, so Layer 3 protocols handle loops and every link can be used simultaneously. That is the whole point of moving away from an all-Layer-2 design.

q: Traffic flowing between two servers inside the same data centre is described as which of the following?
e: East-west is horizontal traffic within the data centre. North-south crosses layers, typically between the data centre and the outside world.

q: A host is configured for DHCP and has the address 169.254.11.7. What does this indicate?
a: The host could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
The DHCP server assigned an address from a depleted secondary scope
The host has a duplicate IP address conflict
e: 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA. The NIC and stack work, but no DHCP server answered — check the server, the scope, the VLAN, or a missing IP helper address.

q: What is the network address for host 192.168.10.100/26?
e: A /26 gives mask 255.255.255.192, so the magic number is 64. Blocks start at 0, 64, 128, 192; 100 falls in the 64 block. Broadcast is .127 and usable range is .65 to .126.

q: Which subnet mask is most efficient for a point-to-point WAN link between two routers?
e: A /30 gives exactly two usable addresses, one per router interface, wasting nothing.

q: When designing a VLSM scheme, in what order should subnets be allocated?
a: In the order departments are listed
e: Largest first. Allocating smallest first fragments the address space and you run out before the large subnets are placed.

q: Which feature of IPv4 does IPv6 eliminate entirely?
e: IPv6 has no broadcast at all. Multicast takes over those functions, and anycast is also supported.

q: How many times may the '::' abbreviation appear in a single IPv6 address?
e: Only once. A second occurrence would make the number of collapsed zero groups ambiguous.

q: In software-defined networking, which function is separated from the physical device and centralised?
e: SDN separates the control plane — the decision-making — into centralised software. The device keeps the data plane and still forwards traffic.

q: An organisation has exhausted the available VLAN IDs in a large multi-tenant environment. Which technology addresses this?
e: 802.1Q caps VLANs at 4,096. VXLAN tunnels Layer 2 frames inside Layer 3 UDP, raising the ceiling to roughly 16 million segments that can also span sites.

q: Which architecture combines SD-WAN with cloud-delivered security functions at the network edge?
e: Secure Access Service Edge bundles SD-WAN with a secure web gateway, firewall as a service, a cloud access security broker, and zero trust network access.

q: Users in two different VLANs can unexpectedly reach each other across a trunk. What should you check first?
a: Whether the native VLAN matches on both ends of the trunk
Whether the switches are running the same IOS version
Whether PortFast is enabled on the trunk
Whether the trunk cable is a crossover
e: A native VLAN mismatch causes untagged traffic from one VLAN to land in another. It is both a connectivity fault and a VLAN hopping risk.

q: A link is up but throughput is very poor, and the interface shows increasing late collisions and CRC errors. What is the most likely cause?
e: Late collisions on a link that stays up is the signature of a duplex mismatch — one side full, the other half. The link never goes down, which is what makes it confusing.

q: Why do Layer 2 switching loops require Spanning Tree Protocol when Layer 3 routing loops resolve themselves?
a: Ethernet frames have no TTL field, so a looping frame circulates forever
Layer 2 has no MAC address table to consult
Layer 3 loops are prevented by ARP
e: IP packets carry a TTL that is decremented at each hop and eventually discards the packet. Ethernet frames have no equivalent, so broadcast frames multiply until the network is saturated.

q: An IP camera mounted outside the building has no nearby power outlet. Which technology solves this?
e: PoE delivers power and data over the same Ethernet cable, which is exactly why it suits cameras and access points in locations without power.

q: A default-configured switch port shuts down and goes into err-disabled state after an unauthorised device is connected. Which violation mode is in effect?
e: Shutdown is the default port security violation mode and requires manual recovery. Restrict drops and logs; protect drops silently.

q: A router has both a static route and an OSPF route to the same prefix with the same prefix length. Which is installed?
a: The static route, because its administrative distance is lower
The OSPF route, because it is dynamically learned
Neither, until the conflict is resolved manually
e: Administrative distance breaks ties between protocols and lower wins. Static is 1, OSPF is 110. A stale static route silently overriding OSPF is a common real-world fault.

q: Which criterion does a router evaluate first when selecting between multiple routes to a destination?
e: Most specific route wins, regardless of protocol or metric. Administrative distance and metric only come into play afterwards.

q: Which first hop redundancy protocol load-balances traffic across multiple routers simultaneously?
e: HSRP and VRRP are active/standby — only one router forwards. GLBP adds genuine load balancing across gateways.

q: Which routing protocol is used between autonomous systems and forms the routing backbone of the internet?
e: BGP is a path-vector exterior gateway protocol. OSPF, EIGRP and RIP are interior gateway protocols operating within an autonomous system.

q: What distinguishes traffic shaping from traffic policing?
a: Shaping buffers and delays excess traffic; policing drops it
Shaping drops excess traffic; policing buffers it
Shaping operates at Layer 2; policing at Layer 3
Shaping applies only to inbound traffic
e: Shaping smooths bursts by queueing, which adds latency. Policing enforces a hard ceiling by discarding or re-marking, which does not.

q: Which channels are the only non-overlapping ones in the 2.4 GHz band in North America?
e: Only 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap. Adjacent access points must use different non-overlapping channels or they degrade each other.

q: What is the fundamental authentication difference between WPA2-Personal and WPA3-Personal?
a: WPA2 uses one pre-shared key for all clients; WPA3 negotiates a separate key per device using SAE
WPA3 uses a pre-shared key while WPA2 uses certificates
WPA2 uses AES and WPA3 uses TKIP
WPA3 authenticates against RADIUS while WPA2 does not
e: With a PSK, cracking the single shared code exposes everyone. WPA3's Simultaneous Authentication of Equals gives each device its own negotiated key, so sessions are independent.

q: An organisation must revoke one departing employee's wireless access without changing anything for other users. What should be deployed?
a: WPA2 or WPA3 Enterprise with 802.1X and RADIUS
WPA2-Personal with a strong pre-shared key
e: Enterprise mode authenticates per user against RADIUS, so a single account can be disabled. A shared passphrase would have to be changed for everyone.

q: A large campus is deploying forty access points that must share one configuration and channel plan. Which type should be used?
a: Lightweight access points managed by a wireless LAN controller
Consumer wireless routers in bridge mode
e: Autonomous APs must each be edited separately, which does not scale. Lightweight APs take their configuration from a controller that also coordinates channels and roaming.

q: Which antenna type would best link two buildings 500 metres apart?
a: A directional antenna such as a Yagi or parabolic dish
A dipole antenna at reduced power
e: Directional antennas trade coverage area for range and gain by focusing the same transmit power into a beam.

q: According to TIA/EIA structured cabling standards, what is the maximum length of the horizontal run from the equipment room to the wall outlet?
e: The budget is 90 m horizontal, 6 m from outlet to computer, and 3 m from patch panel to rack equipment — which is how the familiar 100 m limit is actually apportioned.

q: Why must a data centre HVAC system be able to stop ventilating during a fire?
a: Fans draw too much power during an emergency
e: The oxygen an HVAC system circulates makes a fire worse, so these systems detect fire and halt ventilation.

q: How many broadcast domains does a single switch with four VLANs configured create?
a: Four times the number of ports
e: A switch is one broadcast domain by default, but each VLAN becomes its own broadcast domain requiring a Layer 3 device to route between them.

q: Hosts on one VLAN receive APIPA addresses while every other VLAN gets addressing normally. What is the most likely cause?
a: A missing IP helper address on that VLAN's router interface
The DHCP scope is exhausted network-wide
DNS is misconfigured for that VLAN
e: DHCP Discover is a broadcast and does not cross routers. Without a relay agent or IP helper on that interface, that one subnet cannot reach the server while others can.

q: A printer must always receive the same IP address but remain centrally managed through DHCP. What should be configured?
a: A DHCP reservation tied to the printer's MAC address
A static IP address on the printer itself
An exclusion range covering the printer
A shorter lease duration for the printer
e: A reservation keeps the address consistent while leaving management at the DHCP server, which preserves central visibility.

q: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
e: A is IPv4, AAAA is IPv6, CNAME is an alias to another name, and PTR is used for reverse lookups.

q: A technician shuts down the wrong interface on a remote router and loses all access to it. Which management approach would have prevented being locked out?
e: In-band management depends on the production network you may have just broken. Out-of-band uses a separate path such as a console server or cellular modem, so it survives the outage.

q: Why does inaccurate time on network devices cause authentication failures?
a: Kerberos rejects requests outside a small clock skew tolerance
Passwords expire based on device local time
DNS refuses to resolve names on unsynchronised hosts
DHCP leases cannot be issued without accurate time
e: Kerberos is time-sensitive, and certificate validity checking also depends on accurate time. Log correlation across devices breaks as well, which is why NTP matters more than it appears.

q: Which technology tells you what the traffic on a saturated link actually consists of, rather than just how much there is?
e: SNMP reports interface counters and volume. NetFlow records flows — source, destination, ports, protocol, duration — which answers why the link is saturated.

q: Which SNMP version should be used when the requirement is authenticated and encrypted management traffic?
e: v1 and v2c transmit community strings in cleartext. Only v3 adds authentication and encryption.

q: On the syslog severity scale, which level is the most severe?
e: Zero is most severe and seven is most verbose. Leaving a device at debug level in production can generate enough logging to affect performance.

q: Why is a network performance baseline valuable?
a: It provides a record of normal operation so deviations can be identified and justified
It automatically prevents congestion from occurring
It replaces the need for SNMP monitoring
It guarantees the service level agreement will be met
e: Without a baseline, 'the network is slow' cannot be proven or disproven. With one, you can show a link that normally runs at 30 percent is now at 85.

q: An organisation states that no more than one hour of data may be lost in a disaster. Which metric has been defined?
e: RPO is the tolerance for data loss, measured backwards from the incident, and it drives backup frequency. RTO is the tolerance for downtime.

q: A system operated for 1,000 hours and failed four times. What is its MTBF?
e: MTBF is total operating time divided by number of failures: 1000 divided by 4 equals 250 hours. Higher values indicate greater reliability.

q: A business has an RTO measured in minutes. Which disaster recovery site satisfies that requirement?
a: Any site, provided backups are current
e: Only a hot site, with hardware running and data continuously replicated, recovers in minutes. Warm takes hours to days and cold takes days to weeks.

q: Two NICs are teamed on a server, both connected to the same switch. Which failure does this configuration NOT protect against?
e: Teaming into a single switch leaves that switch as a single point of failure. Homing the team into two different switches covers the larger failure domain.

q: Which backup type requires the last full backup plus only the most recent backup of its own type to restore?
e: Differential captures everything changed since the last full, so restore needs just the full plus the latest differential. Incremental restores need the full plus every incremental since.

q: A product has reached end of life but not yet end of support. What does this mean?
a: It is no longer sold but still receives limited updates
It receives no further updates of any kind
It has been recalled by the manufacturer
It can no longer be legally operated
e: End of life means the product is no longer sold. End of support, often two or more years later, means no more updates or patches at all — which is when unpatched vulnerabilities become permanent.

q: Which wireless site survey type requires actually connecting to the access point?
e: Passive measures signal strength, coverage and interference without associating. Active connects and measures throughput, packet loss and data rates — showing whether data is actually getting through.

q: An outage is traced to an undocumented hardware swap performed without approval. Which process failed?
e: Change management exists to plan, test, approve and document changes so they do not cause unexpected disruption — including defining a rollback plan before work begins.

q: Which tool centrally manages DHCP and DNS servers and monitors address pool utilisation across an organisation?
e: IP Address Management presents multiple DHCP and DNS servers through a single interface and alerts on pool exhaustion before users start seeing APIPA addresses.

q: Which security principle does hashing protect?
e: Hashing is one-way and verifies that data has not been altered. Encryption protects confidentiality; redundancy protects availability.

q: Why does TLS use both asymmetric and symmetric cryptography?
a: Asymmetric exchanges the session key; symmetric encrypts the bulk data because it is far faster
Asymmetric encrypts the data and symmetric verifies the certificate
Symmetric is used for the handshake and asymmetric for the payload
Both are used identically for redundancy
e: Asymmetric cryptography solves key distribution but is slow. Once a symmetric session key has been exchanged, the bulk transfer uses the faster symmetric algorithm.

q: A deliberately vulnerable system is deployed to observe attacker behaviour and tune intrusion detection. What is it?
e: A honeypot is a virtual trap. The intelligence gathered helps configure automated detection and reduce false positives.

q: Which access control method authenticates an identity rather than a hardware address?
e: MAC addresses travel in cleartext and are trivially spoofed. 802.1X authenticates a user or device credential against a RADIUS server before opening the port.

q: An ACL is not blocking traffic that a specific deny rule addresses. What should you check?
a: Whether a permit rule appears above the deny rule
Whether the ACL has been saved to startup configuration
Whether the interface is running at the correct duplex
Whether the ACL uses IPv4 or IPv6 syntax
e: ACLs are processed top to bottom and the first match wins, so a permissive rule placed above a restrictive one makes the restrictive rule unreachable.

q: Which AAA protocol encrypts the entire payload and separates authentication, authorisation and accounting?
e: RADIUS encrypts only the password and combines authentication with authorisation. TACACS+ encrypts everything and separates all three, which is why it is preferred for device administration.

q: Which physical control specifically prevents tailgating?
e: A mantrap or access control vestibule uses two interlocking doors so only one person passes at a time. Cameras are detective, not preventative.

q: A technician needs to change a switch's default password. Which method is acceptable?
a: Over SSH or a console connection
e: Telnet and HTTP transmit in cleartext, so changing a password over them exposes the new credential immediately. Use SSH or direct console access.

q: What is the practical difference between a firewall rule that drops traffic and one that rejects it?
a: A drop is silent and produces a timeout; a reject sends notification and fails immediately
A drop logs the attempt while a reject does not
A drop applies inbound and a reject applies outbound
e: Dropping reveals nothing to a scanner but gives legitimate users confusing timeouts. Rejecting fails fast and clearly but confirms the host exists.

q: An access point's signal reaches well into the car park. What should be adjusted?
e: Excess transmit power extends your attack surface geographically. Tune power so coverage matches the space you intend to serve.

q: What is the recommended approach for a fleet of IoT devices with default credentials and no patch path?
a: Place them on a segmented VLAN with tightly restricted access
Place them on the same VLAN as workstations for easier monitoring
Assign each a public IP address for remote management
e: Segmentation contains devices you cannot properly secure, limiting what an attacker reaches after compromising one.

q: You have just tested your theory and confirmed the cause. According to the CompTIA methodology, what is the next step?
a: Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects
e: The order is identify, theorise, test, plan, implement, verify, document. Planning sits between confirming the cause and implementing the fix.

q: A technician replaces a suspect cable and leaves without checking. Which step of the methodology was skipped?
a: Testing the theory to determine the cause
Establishing a theory of probable cause
e: A theory must be validated. Installing a new cable and walking away assumes the theory was right — if the user still cannot connect, the theory was actually disproved.

q: A user can access internal file shares and printers but not the internet. Which troubleshooting approach is most efficient?
a: Top-down, starting with DNS and application-layer services
Bottom-up, starting with the cable and NIC
e: Working access to internal resources eliminates the physical and data link layers entirely, so starting at the top finds the fault fastest.

q: Internet access is lost for one host. Which single failure is statistically more likely?
a: The default gateway, because most clients have only one
Both configured DNS servers failing simultaneously
The client's NIC and its cable failing together
e: Prioritise by likelihood, not just possibility. Most clients have two DNS servers but only one default gateway, so a single gateway failure is far more probable.

q: Why should failed corrective actions be recorded in troubleshooting documentation?
a: So a future technician does not waste time repeating them
To assign responsibility for the failed attempt
Because compliance frameworks require a failure log
e: The knowledge base is only useful if it records what did not work as well as what did. That is half its value.

q: A successful ping to 127.0.0.1 proves what?
a: TCP/IP is correctly installed and bound to the local adapter
e: The loopback address tests the local TCP/IP stack without touching the network. Success rules out the local adapter as the cause.

q: Which tool identifies a break in a copper cable and reports the distance to the fault?
e: A TDR reports distance to the fault, so you can go to the spot instead of replacing the entire run. A tester only confirms continuity and pinout.

q: What does a cable certifier do that a cable tester does not?
a: Verifies the run meets a performance standard such as Cat 6 at its rated speed
Locates the far end of a cable in a bundle
Detects the presence of PoE voltage
e: A cable can pass continuity testing and still fail to carry gigabit reliably. Certification tests against the performance specification.

q: Ping succeeds but large file transfers hang or fail across a particular path. What should you investigate?
a: An MTU mismatch along the path
e: Small packets pass while large ones are fragmented or black-holed when the Don't Fragment bit is set. Test with ping using the DF flag and varying sizes to find the real path MTU.

q: A DHCP scope was configured as 192.168.1.100 to 192.168.1.200, and a server already uses 192.168.1.150 statically. What will happen?
a: A duplicate IP address conflict when that address is leased
The DHCP server will detect and skip the address automatically
The static host will lose its address at the next renewal
Nothing, because static addresses take precedence
e: The scope must exclude any statically assigned addresses inside its range. Otherwise the server will eventually lease .150 to a client and both hosts will have connectivity problems.

q: Which condition describes signal from one wire inside an Ethernet cable being picked up by another wire in the same cable?
e: Crosstalk refers to the individual conductors inside one cable, not two cables run alongside each other. Common causes include damage near the connector and too much copper exposed during crimping.

q: A connection attempt times out rather than being refused immediately. What does this suggest?
a: A device in the path is silently dropping the traffic
No service is listening on that port
e: A timeout points to something discarding traffic silently, typically a firewall configured to drop. An immediate refusal means the packet reached a host that actively said no.

q: Guest wireless users in a busy conference centre stop receiving addresses by mid-morning, though the scope is large. What should be adjusted?
e: In high-turnover environments long leases keep addresses reserved for devices that have already left, exhausting the pool. Shorter leases return addresses sooner.

q: A browser reports a certificate error after a web server was renamed. What is the most likely cause?
a: A name mismatch between the server and the name on its certificate
The certificate's private key was deleted
The root CA revoked the certificate
The server's cipher suite is unsupported
e: Renaming a server so that its name no longer matches the certificate invalidates the certificate entirely. Incorrect system time causes a similar symptom for a different reason.

q: Several unrelated devices fail at the same moment in the same rack. What should you investigate first?
a: A shared upstream cause such as power, cooling or a common uplink
Each device individually, starting with the oldest
e: Determining scope is step one of the methodology. Simultaneous widespread failure almost always has one shared cause rather than many coincidental ones.

q: An attacker floods a switch with frames carrying thousands of forged source MAC addresses. What is the consequence once the MAC address table fills?
a: The switch floods frames out every port, letting the attacker see other hosts' traffic
The switch reboots and clears its configuration
All VLANs merge into a single broadcast domain
Spanning Tree recalculates and blocks the attacker's port
e: MAC flooding exhausts the CAM table so the switch can no longer look up destinations and reverts to hub-like flooding. An availability attack that becomes a confidentiality attack. Port security is the control.

q: Which control specifically defends against a rogue DHCP server?
e: DHCP snooping permits DHCP server responses only from trusted ports. DAI addresses ARP poisoning and DNSSEC addresses DNS poisoning.

q: An attacker crafts a frame with two 802.1Q tags so the first switch strips the outer tag and the second delivers it into a different VLAN. What is this, and what prevents it?
a: Double tagging, prevented by using an unused native VLAN
Switch spoofing, prevented by disabling trunk negotiation
MAC flooding, prevented by port security
e: Double tagging exploits the native VLAN, which crosses trunks untagged. Setting the native VLAN to an unused one defeats it. It is also one-way — the attacker receives nothing back.

q: Hosts on a subnet show the default gateway's IP mapped to an unexpected MAC address, and the same MAC appears for several IPs. What is happening?
a: ARP poisoning positioning an on-path attacker
e: ARP has no authentication, so an attacker can claim the gateway's IP. Two IPs resolving to one MAC is the detection signature. Dynamic ARP Inspection is the control.

q: What distinguishes a worm from a virus?
a: A worm self-replicates across the network with no user interaction
A worm attaches itself to an executable file
A worm always encrypts data and demands payment
A worm only runs in memory and never touches disk
e: A virus needs a user to open or run something. A worm needs nothing, which is why worms spread so fast. Rapid spread with no user action means worm.

q: An attacker sends small spoofed queries to public DNS servers so that large responses are directed at a victim. What is this technique?
e: The attacker spoofs the victim's address as the source, so replies go to the victim. A small query producing a large answer multiplies the attacker's own bandwidth.

q: A WAN link becomes unusable during a nightly backup window. No malicious activity is found. How is this best classified?
a: An unintentional or friendly denial of service
e: Not every outage is an attack. Legitimate traffic saturating a link, or a misconfiguration causing a loop, produces denial of service without an attacker.

q: Which social engineering attack targets executives specifically?
e: Whaling is spear phishing aimed at high-value individuals such as executives. Vishing is by voice, smishing by SMS, and pretexting invents a scenario to establish false legitimacy.

q: Which backup practice is the meaningful defence against ransomware?
a: An offline or immutable copy that the attacker cannot encrypt
Storing backups on the same SAN as production
Compressing backups to reduce restore time
e: An attacker who can reach and encrypt your backups has defeated the strategy entirely. Offline or immutable copies are what survive, which is the point of the off-site element of 3-2-1.

q: An attacker connects a device that negotiates a trunk link with a switch, gaining access to all VLANs. What prevents this?
a: Explicitly configuring access ports and disabling trunk negotiation
Enabling PortFast on all access ports
Increasing the MAC address table size
Enabling BPDU Guard on trunk links
e: Switch spoofing works because the port will negotiate a trunk. Setting ports explicitly to access mode and disabling dynamic negotiation removes the opportunity.

q: A user reaches a site with the correct name in the address bar, but the browser reports a certificate error and the page looks wrong. What is most likely?
a: DNS poisoning redirecting the name to an attacker's address
A duplex mismatch on the path
e: The attacker can redirect the name but cannot produce a valid certificate for it, so the warning fires. That warning is the user's last line of defence, which is why training people to click through it is damaging.

q: Which attack tries one common password across many accounts rather than many passwords against one account?
e: Spraying avoids triggering account lockout by limiting attempts per account. Credential stuffing reuses credentials leaked from a different breach.

q: A remote worker's VPN is configured so that only corporate-bound traffic goes through the tunnel while internet traffic goes direct. What is this, and what is the trade-off?
a: Split tunnel — better performance, but direct traffic is uninspected
Full tunnel — better security, but higher bandwidth cost
Site-to-site — simpler routing, but no client control
Clientless — easier deployment, but no encryption
e: Split tunnelling avoids backhauling internet traffic through headquarters, but anything going direct bypasses corporate inspection. Full tunnel inspects everything at the cost of performance.

q: Why is a jump server considered both a strong control and a significant risk?
a: It concentrates administrative access into one hardened, audited chokepoint — which also makes it a high-value single point of failure
It encrypts all traffic but cannot log sessions
It replaces the need for multi-factor authentication
It only works for Linux hosts
e: Funnelling administrative access through one monitored host reduces attack surface and centralises logging. Compromise it and you have compromised the path to everything behind it.

q: Ping times to a VoIP server are consistently low, yet users report choppy, broken audio. What should you investigate?
a: Jitter — variation in packet arrival time
e: Average latency can look excellent while calls are unusable, because voice depends on consistency of arrival rather than average speed. Good ping plus bad call quality points at jitter.

q: A gigabit link shows low utilisation but transfers achieve only a fraction of the expected speed. What should you check first?
a: Interface error counters and duplex settings
Whether the link needs upgrading to 10 Gbps
e: Bandwidth and throughput are different measures. A gap between them points to duplex mismatch, retransmissions, MTU problems or device CPU — not to needing a bigger link.
